chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Take the Mus'haf (Quran) during the second third of the month of Ramadan, so display it and place it in front of you and say:

O Allah, I ask You by Your Revealed Book and what is in it, and in it is Your Greatest Name, the Magnificent, and Your Good Names, and what is feared and hoped for, that You make me from those emancipated by You from the Fire,
and supplicate with whatever seems fit to you regarding your needs.

key_terms.اسْمُكَ الْأَعْظَمُ: Your Greatest Name, a concept in Islamic theology referring to a name of God through which supplications are answered
key_terms.الثُّلُثِ الثَّانِي: The second third of a period, specifically referring to the 11th-20th days of Ramadan in this context
key_terms.الْمُصْحَف: The physical copy or parchment of the Quran
key_terms.عُتَقَائِكَ: Your emancipated ones, those freed by God

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite with the Quran during the second third of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) prescribes a specific devotional practice for the second third of Ramadan, emphasizing the Quran as a tangible medium for intercession (shifa' and wasilah) through the invocation of Allah's Greatest Name (Ism al-A'zam). In Shia tradition, this ritual highlights the spiritual potency of the Quranic text itself, linking the attributes of fear and hope to the ultimate goal of liberation from the Hellfire, a concept deeply rooted in the theological understanding of divine mercy and justice.
